papers.title: Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that complete expanding K\"ahler-Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in Stein manifolds, and hence pseudoconvexity of bounded domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete K\"ahler-Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.

papers.title: Wolff-type ideal theorems for slice regular functions
papers.abstract: We study Wolff-type ideal problems in $H^\infty(\mathbb B)$, the algebra of bounded slice regular functions on the quaternionic unit ball. We construct $f,f_1,f_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb B)$ satisfying $|f|^2\le |f_1|^2+|f_2|^2$ such that $f^{\ast N}\notin\mathcal I(f_1,f_2)$ for every integer $N\ge1$, where $\mathcal I(f_1,f_2)$ denotes the right ideal generated by $f_1$ and $f_2$. We also construct intrinsic functions $a,a_1,a_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb B)$ satisfying $|a|\le |a_1|+|a_2|\le1$ and $a^{\ast2}\notin\mathcal I(a_1,a_2)$. For intrinsic data satisfying $|f|\le\sum_{\ell=1}^n|f_\ell|$, the cube $f^{\ast3}$ has a representation in the generated right ideal with intrinsic coefficients. For general data, we obtain sufficient conditions for ideal membership under a fourth-order pointwise bound with a Dini factor. If the generators preserve a common slice, a quadratic bound with a Dini factor suffices.

papers.title: On the solution of a question for meromorphic functions sharing three values IM and a fourth value CM in the complex plane
papers.abstract: In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a M\"{o}bius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

papers.title: Nondefective lifts of stationary discs and the 2-jet determination problem
papers.abstract: We introduce a natural notion of defect for lifts of stationary discs attached to a CR nondegenerate submanifold $M \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ of codimension $d$. We prove that the existence of a nondefective lift of a stationary disc implies that germs of CR automorphisms of $M$ are uniquely determined by their $2$-jet. We emphasize that, in particular, this unifies all previously known results on this question.

papers.title: Mateability of Fuchsian lattices with polynomials, and failure of algebraicity
papers.abstract: We prove that all Fuchsian lattices, with the possible exceptions of those associated with compact orbifolds of type (0,3) and (1,1), can be mated with complex polynomials, providing the first examples of such combinations beyond genus-zero orbifolds. We also present the first construction of matings between simply degenerate Kleinian groups and polynomial maps. These matings are realized as holomorphic, though not necessarily algebraic, correspondences, demonstrating that Fatou's vision of unifying Kleinian group actions and polynomial dynamics can be fulfilled in the wider setting of transcendental correspondences. We achieve this by generalizing the orbit equivalence mating framework introduced in our earlier work. Specifically, we use pinching and acceleration techniques to construct a new class of piecewise M\"obius covering maps of the circle that are orbit equivalent to Fuchsian groups. By mating these circle coverings with polynomials, we construct degenerate polynomial-like maps whose analytic continuations yield the desired correspondences. The quality of this orbit equivalence plays a crucial role in the mating description, as well as in governing whether the resulting correspondences are algebraic.

papers.title: Matrix-point interpolation for positive real odd functions in one and several variables
papers.abstract: We study the single matrix point interpolation problem for positive real matrix valued functions on the right half-plane, both in the single variable setting and in the noncommutative multivariable setting. In the single variable case, a careful analysis is done for when the solution may or must have a pole at infinity. In the multivariable setting, as the pole structure at infinity can be more complicated, we focus on the case when there is no pole at infinity. The results also yield numerical algorithms for finding a solution.

papers.title: Polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces and the polyanalytic $q$-Bargmann transform
papers.abstract: We study polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces from an operator-theoretic point of view. We compute the formal adjoint $A^*$ of the Jackson derivative $A=\overline{R}_{q}$ on the polynomials in $z,\overline{z}$ inside $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},\mu_{q})$ and we show that, up to unimodular factors, a twist by the grading operator is the only modification of $A$ diagonal in the grading for which a deformed canonical relation $aa^*-\lambda a^*a=I$ holds. The resulting second-order $q$-difference operator $a^*a$ is essentially self-adjoint on the polynomials and $q$-complex Hermite polynomials span its eigenspaces. These eigenspaces give the orthogonal decomposition of $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},\mu_{q})$ into true polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces. We determine the disk on which each of them is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and we factor the corresponding unitary $q$-Bargmann transforms through powers of $a^*$.

papers.title: Remark on Kobayashi's conjecture: a volume Schwarz lemma
papers.abstract: This remark offers an expository reconstruction of OpenAI's proof of Kobayashi's ampleness conjecture for compact K\"ahler manifolds, together with new results. We extract a volume Schwarz lemma for extremal discs and derive a pointwise volume comparison: the volume form of a K\"ahler metric with $\mathrm{Ric}(\omega)\ge-\omega$ is bounded below by an intrinsic volume form built from the K\"ahler--Einstein metrics of pseudoconvex domains containing the Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix. As a consequence, if a compact K\"ahler manifold $X$ has nef canonical bundle and its Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix is bounded at some point, then $X$ is of general type.
